newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Warburg sees CANTV slump as buying opportunity.
newsitem.headline: Warburg sees CANTV slump as buying opportunity.

text.p: SBC Warburg sees a nearly 20 percent slump in two weeks of Venezuelan telephone company CANTV stock as a buying opportunity, the investment house's Latin American telecoms analyst Zaine Manekia said.

"We think a valuation below $28 very attractive," Manekia told Reuters in a telephone interview. The stock's American Depository Receipt closed Tuesday at 27-3/8 and has traded down Wednesday, dipping as low as 26-1/2 in strong volume.
Warburg underwrote the company's one billion dollar November global share offering with investment house Lehman Brothers.
"The company's currently trading at 5.1 times estimated 1997 EBITDA, which is a significant discount to its peers, which are at 6.2 times," he said.
"Over the long term we think CANTV a great buy," he added.

CANTV stock has slid from a Feb. 26 high of 33-3/4 on investor concern with a delayed second quarter tariff increase and an indefinite workers' strike, set for Thursday, over a 154 percent pay rise spread over two years.
Commenting on the share price drop, Maneika said: "We feel there's been a lot of misinformation and misinterpretation."
Maneika added he felt good progress was being made in talks with both the unions and the Ministry of Transport and Communications, public noises to the contrary.
"There are some sticky issues with the rates rebalancing," he said. "But we feel the company's September 1996 agreement (with the Ministry and telecommunication authority, Conatel) will stick."
